name: format.yearqtr
title: An Index Class for Quarterly Data

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A yearqtr, or a value as.yearqtr can coerce.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A string. %C, %Y, %y, and %q are the century, year, two-digit year, and quarter.

origin.details: The default "%Y Q%q" pastes the year, a space, Q, and the quarter. Any other format replaces %q, then %Y, then %y, then %C. %y is two digits. A missing yearqtr stays missing. The year is floor(x + 0.001) and the quarter is floor(4 * (x - year) + 1.501).
origin.example:
x <- as.yearqtr(2000 + seq(0, 7)/4)
cat(paste(format(x, "%Y Quarter %q"), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(format(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A Yearqtr, or a value as_yearqtr can coerce.

arguments.name: format
arguments.text: A string. %C, %Y, %y, and %q become the century, year, two-digit year, and quarter.

translation.details: "%Y Q%q" is pasted directly. Any other string replaces %q, then %Y, then %y, then %C, in that order. %y is printed with two digits. A missing value stays missing. A format longer than one string raises ValueError, matching R 4.5.
translation.value: A list of strings. A missing quarter is None.
translation.example:
import numpy as np
from zoo.yearqtr import as_yearqtr, format_yearqtr
x = as_yearqtr(2000 + np.arange(8) / 4)
print(" ".join(format_yearqtr(x, "%Y Quarter %q")))
print(" ".join(format_yearqtr(x)))
